title: Acquired glory belongs to the man of Christ, not to Father or Word
english: The Father does not receive acquired glory, for he is perfect, infinite, incomprehensible, and without need of beauty and every seemliness. Nor does his Word receive it, for he is God begotten from the Father, through whom angels and heavens and the boundless expanses of the earth have come to be, and in short all the materials and constitutions of created things. Rather, it is the man of Christ who, being raised from the dead, is exalted and glorified, while his enemies openly took up shame. Those who took up hatred against him out of envy and were fenced in by a hostile battle-line are scattered, since the Word and God has fittingly raised his own temple.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is explaining why the Psalms of Ascents speak of glory being given: it cannot belong to the Father or the Word, but only to the man of Christ raised from the dead.
